fixes.explanation: Moses, Israel's leader, doesn't mention an altar here. What he says is that they and their children “…return to the LORD your God and obey His voice with all your heart and all your soul…” The verse is about turning back to the LORD. Keep your eyes on that.

Moses says the opposite. He says the LORD “…will bring you into the land your fathers possessed, and you will take possession of it.” Then he adds, “He will cause you to prosper and multiply more than your fathers.” So the promise is more than their fathers had, not less. It's easy to flip a word when you're moving fast. I've read a recipe backwards myself.

Yes, False. Moses says the LORD will bring them into the land their fathers possessed. Then comes the lift: “He will cause you to prosper and multiply more than your fathers.” Their fathers set the bar, and the promise goes over it.

Yes! Moses says the LORD “…will circumcise your hearts and the hearts of your descendants, and you will love Him with all your heart and with all your soul, so that you may live.” Notice who does the circumcising: the LORD. The love is what Moses says the people will do after that. And it ends with “…so that you may live.”

Nothing in this verse says they forget. Moses actually has them calling the blessings and curses to mind in verse 1. What he says comes after the LORD circumcises their hearts is love, with all their heart and with all their soul. And that love is tied to living.

That promise isn't in this verse. Moses names something else. After the LORD circumcises their hearts, they will love Him with all their heart and with all their soul, so that they may live. Staying put forever isn't part of what he says here.

Share is a nice word, friend, and I'd hand you a cookie for the effort. But Moses says the LORD will again delight in their prosperity, just as He delighted in that of their fathers. Delight is the word. It tells you how the LORD feels, not what He divides up.

The city gate is a fair guess, friend, but Moses doesn't send anyone there. He says the word is very near them, in their mouth and in their heart. No gate, no waiting line, no appointment. I've waited in lines for less.

That's the life side. Moses says, “For I am commanding you today to love the LORD your God, to walk in His ways, and to keep His commandments, statutes, and ordinances…” Love the LORD, walk in His ways, keep His commandments. That's the command in Moses' own words.

Gold and strong cities sound impressive, friend, but they aren't in this command. Moses commands them to love the LORD their God, to walk in His ways, and to keep His commandments, statutes, and ordinances. That's his list, and nobody needs a vault for it.

Every single morning sounds like a lot of snooze buttons getting hit, friend. But a daily sacrifice isn't what Moses names here. He commands them to love the LORD their God, to walk in His ways, and to keep His commandments, statutes, and ordinances.

That's what Moses declares. He says, “…you will surely perish; you shall not prolong your days in the land that you are crossing the Jordan to possess.” It comes after he describes a heart that turns away and bows down to other gods. It's a heavy line, and I think it hits hard.

Flocks don't come up in that warning, friend. Moses declares that they will surely perish, and that they shall not prolong their days in the land they're crossing the Jordan to possess. This is a heavy part. I think it's worth slowing down for.

Forty more years isn't in this warning. Moses declares that if their heart turns away to other gods, they will surely perish and not prolong their days in the land. That's a heavy one, so I'll leave it right where Moses put it.

Priests and Levites are a fair guess, friend, but Moses calls a bigger crew. He says, “I call heaven and earth as witnesses against you today…” Heaven and earth. That's a witness list with no empty seats.

Only the elders and leaders would be a short guest list, friend, but Moses says more. He tells them, “Therefore choose life, so that you and your descendants may live…” You and your descendants. The choice isn't just for the leaders.

The nations around them would be a big crowd, but that isn't who Moses names. He says, “…so that you and your descendants may live…” That's the people he's speaking to and their descendants. Moses keeps the circle close.

Shield sounds strong, friend, but it isn't the word in this verse. Moses wants them to love the LORD, obey Him and hold fast to Him. Then he gives the reason: “For He is your life…” Life, not shield. That's hard to beat.
